summary.title: Android Platform-aware Black-box STRIDE - Clear Labels
summary.description:
Platform-aware black-box STRIDE reference; 28 October 2026.
The physical device is owned and controlled by the tester. Device/OS architecture
is known platform context, not an opaque assessment target. Record the actual
model, OS/build, security patch, lock/passcode, backup, permissions, pairing and
debug settings in device-profile.txt before applying this template to a target.
These values are not supplied yet. Ownership does not imply root/jailbreak,
permission to bypass sandbox isolation, or an already compromised OS.

Only the mobile app is opaque within the device. No app-specific internal layers,
libraries, algorithms or business logic are asserted. The remote service is also
opaque, as requested: no database, internal logs or server configuration is drawn.
Remote communication is a supplied baseline assumption. Exact calls, endpoint
count, protocol, TLS, authentication, roles and feature availability must be
established by observation. App and server controls are unverified.

Known device facilities are expanded: OS entry dispatch, an app-private file
namespace, permission-controlled system resources, and iOS Keychain or Android
Keystore. Their availability is platform knowledge; the app's use and configured
policies are unknown. D1 represents an OS-provided private storage location, not
an assertion about a database or persistence framework. App-private files and the opaque app share the B2 sandbox enclosure.
B4 highlights file-access policy inside that enclosure.

Solid lines describe baseline external interactions and the known OS delivery
route, subject to entry availability. Dashed straight lines with * mark candidate
app-to-platform relationships only; remove any not observed/applicable. They do
not assert that this app uses a permission, Keychain/Keystore or particular files.
F03/F08 external entry also requires discovery. Each arrow label is centered on
its own line with a white backing. Only an arrow's own label may cover its line. All exact payloads are unknown.
Permission and key services are logical platform security responsibilities, not
claims about one OS executable process or separate physical hardware.

Tester-owned device inspection, settings changes, companion test apps and permitted
traffic observation can establish target facts. No categorical exclusion of binary
analysis or instrumentation is imposed by the term black-box. Available techniques
and their privileges must be recorded. Baseline adversaries are an ordinary user,
an ordinary other-app identity, and an independent network/API caller. Privileged
local manipulation and compromised OS scenarios are explicit conditional variants;
results obtained only there must not be reported as ordinary sandbox bypasses.

Every threat is an untested candidate, Open/severity TBD. No app has been tested.
Platform facts are distinguished from observed target facts (none yet), conditional
assumptions and unknowns. Proposed mitigations do not describe implemented controls.
Visible operation references alone cannot verify backend audit integrity. Private
file or key access can be limited despite device ownership; record limitations.
Network encryption and store flags are UNVERIFIED placeholders where false, not
findings of cleartext, no integrity protection or absence of credentials. Local
platform flows are OS APIs, not claims of a network protocol or TLS requirement.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T24: An external caller is delegated the app authority
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: An ordinary other app may use an exposed route to trigger privileged app behaviour under the target app identity.

Preconditions: An accessible target entry exists; no assumption that every app exports a route.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: Use a companion test app/browser with ordinary privileges to invoke discovered entries. Compare account state, route verification, caller restrictions and resulting actions. Device ownership is not the caller privilege.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/risks/android-exported
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Restrict exposed entry surfaces and check caller, target resource and user authority before performing protected actions.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T01: Another device operator continues an existing identity
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If protected sessions exist, a person operating the device may act under a previous user's identity.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Observe who can resume protected UI after inactivity, user change or the app's supported lock/logout sequence.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: OWASP MASVS
https://mas.owasp.org/MASVS/

Device scope: tester-owned and inspectable; available observation privileges must be recorded. App and backend internals remain unknown. Platform/service use is conditional until established.
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Define proportionate session expiry and reauthentication for sensitive operations.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T02: Sensitive output is visible outside the intended interaction
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: Private values may be exposed on screens, app-switcher previews or copy/paste paths available to the observer.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Inspect only externally available display, backgrounding and clipboard behaviour using test data.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: OWASP MASVS
https://mas.owasp.org/MASVS/

Device scope: tester-owned and inspectable; available observation privileges must be recorded. App and backend internals remain unknown. Platform/service use is conditional until established.
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Minimize visible sensitive data and apply platform-appropriate display/clipboard handling.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T03: External entry parameters cause an unintended state change
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If F03 exists, a crafted input may change a destination or action beyond the intended entry behaviour.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Compare permitted and unexpected route/input values through an exposed entry path; record visible or remote effects.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: Android Externally Accessible Components
https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/risks/android-exported

Device scope: tester-owned and inspectable; available observation privileges must be recorded. App and backend internals remain unknown. Platform/service use is conditional until established.
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Constrain accepted input, destinations and actions at each exposed entry point.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T04: External input makes the app unavailable
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If an external entry path exists, malformed or oversized input may cause a repeatable crash or hang.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Use bounded, authorized input variations and record availability/recovery without inspecting internal code.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: OWASP Denial of Service
https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Denial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet.html

Device scope: tester-owned and inspectable; available observation privileges must be recorded. App and backend internals remain unknown. Platform/service use is conditional until established.
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Bound processing and input sizes and handle invalid input with recoverable errors.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T05: External Android entry invokes a protected action
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If an external entry surface exists, a caller may trigger a protected operation without the required user authority.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Exercise discovered externally invocable intents/links in logged-out and authorized test-user states; compare protected outcomes.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: Android Externally Accessible Components
https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/risks/android-exported

Device scope: tester-owned and inspectable; available observation privileges must be recorded. App and backend internals remain unknown. Platform/service use is conditional until established.
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Enforce access for externally triggered actions and require user confirmation where appropriate; confirm platform entry restrictions in a separate design review.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T06: A disputed sensitive action lacks reliable attribution evidence
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: Where accountability is required, an actor may deny a sensitive action and available evidence may not distinguish who initiated it.

Evidence to seek: correlate test account, action, timestamp and operation reference across user-visible outcomes and observable requests. A confirmation alone is not proof of actor identity or nonrepudiation. Backend audit records and their integrity remain unknown.

Assessment state: untested; applicable only where an accountable action exists.
Reference: OWASP Logging
https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html
threats.mitigation: Proposed treatment: establish appropriate authenticated action attribution and protected audit evidence; give users useful operation references. Verify internal evidence separately before claiming nonrepudiation.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T07: The app accepts an impostor remote endpoint
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: A network adversary may impersonate the endpoint if the app accepts an invalid server identity.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Where an authorized test path permits, observe rejection of an invalid endpoint identity; otherwise mark this unverified without weakening the target's protections.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: Android Network Security Configuration
https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/security-config

Device scope: tester-owned and inspectable; available observation privileges must be recorded. App and backend internals remain unknown. Platform/service use is conditional until established.
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Require secure transport with appropriate hostname/certificate validation.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T08: A previous user's private content remains accessible
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If accounts exist, private output may remain visible after logout or after switching test users.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Use two test identities and observe screens/navigation after the app's supported logout, relaunch or account switch. Do not infer where residual data is stored.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: OWASP MASVS
https://mas.owasp.org/MASVS/

Device scope: tester-owned and inspectable; available observation privileges must be recorded. App and backend internals remain unknown. Platform/service use is conditional until established.
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Clear or restrict stale user-visible state and reauthorize protected retrievals.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T25: Device logs or diagnostics contain sensitive app data
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: The app may write credentials, personal data or protected response values to device-visible logs/diagnostics.

Preconditions: Platform interaction must be present and relevant assets identified; no failure is assumed.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: With test values, inspect logs/diagnostics accessible in the actual tester-owned setup; record access requirements and release/debug build differences. Do not assume all apps or ordinary other apps can read system logs.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://mas.owasp.org/MASVS/
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Avoid logging secrets and minimize or redact sensitive diagnostic content.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.

threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If authorization boundaries exist, an independent caller may exceed their permitted object, role or operation scope.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Compare equivalent requests using separately owned test resources and identities; verify returned data and state changes.

threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If a non-idempotent action exists, retrying an accepted request may apply an unintended duplicate change.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Repeat a bounded test operation and compare response references plus externally visible resulting state.

threats.description:
Candidate scenario: Unbounded request volume, size or expensive operations may make the remote interface unavailable.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Assess documented limits and bounded, explicitly authorized rate/size behaviour. Do not infer internal resource topology or conduct disruptive load tests by default.

Assessment state: no app-specific observations yet. Features and preconditions must be established before treating this as applicable.
Reference: OWASP Denial of Service

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

Candidate scenario: Where accountability is required, ambiguous replies or missing operation references may prevent correlating a disputed request with its outcome.

Evidence to seek on the tester-owned device / remote interface: Observe returned references, status and test-user-visible history where offered. Absence of such evidence does not prove absence of internal logging.

Closure: record relevant observed behaviour and residual risk. Internal controls not externally verifiable remain unknown and require additional evidence; do not claim them verified from this model.

text.text:
D1 App-private files
OS-provided namespace
Contents / use unknown

data.name:
D1 App-private files
OS-provided namespace
Contents / use unknown
data.description: [PLATFORM FACT] A private app file namespace is provided by the OS. [UNKNOWN APP] Actual persistence, file contents, database use, backup inclusion and protection settings need evidence. Separate drawing does not create a new identity from P1. No direct access for ordinary other apps is implied. False store flags are unverified placeholders.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T19: Sensitive persisted data is recoverable beyond its intended lifetime
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: Sensitive values may remain in app files or included backups beyond the intended lock, logout, retention or account boundary.

Preconditions: App persists sensitive data; observer has a specified file/backup access path. Ordinary other apps are not assumed to read private files.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: Using test data, inspect accessible app artifacts and available backups; compare lock/logout/account states. Record whether file or backup access requires pairing, debug, root/jailbreak or another privilege. Lack of access does not prove no persistence.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/app-specific
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Minimize persisted sensitive data, apply suitable platform file/backup policies and remove or rebind stale user data.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T20: Modified local state influences a protected decision
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: Altered persisted app state may be trusted for identity, entitlement, destinations or queued operations.

Preconditions: App reads local state and the test variant grants a documented modification capability; ownership alone is not sufficient.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: If file modification is available in the tester-owned environment, vary benign test state and observe effects. Label privileged-only results separately from ordinary-user attacks.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/app-specific
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Treat restored state as untrusted and enforce protected decisions at the authoritative service.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T21: Storage exhaustion or corrupt app state prevents recovery
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: Growing cached data, full-device storage or corrupt persisted state may prevent startup or normal use.

Preconditions: Platform interaction must be present and relevant assets identified; no failure is assumed.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: Use bounded test data and controlled low-storage conditions on the owned device; assess recovery without risking unrelated personal data.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Denial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet.html
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Bound retention and processing; handle invalid state and low storage with recoverable errors.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.

P4 Android permission gate
Protected OS resources
data.description: [PLATFORM FACT] OS mediates access to protected device resources. [CONDITIONAL] App requests, grants, accessed resources and resulting behaviour remain unknown. This is a logical gate, not an asserted single process. Specific sensors/features are intentionally unselected.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T22: An OS permission exposes more user data than the feature requires
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: App access to a protected resource may collect or retain more data than the visible purpose requires, or move it to the remote service.

Preconditions: Platform interaction must be present and relevant assets identified; no failure is assumed.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: Inventory actual permission grants and OS privacy indicators/settings; exercise grant, denial and revocation; compare visible behaviour and observable outbound data. A granted permission alone is not a vulnerability.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://mas.owasp.org/MASVS/
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Request proportionate access at the point of need and limit collection, retention and transmission.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T23: Permission denial or revocation makes the app unusable
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: The app may fail repeatedly when a requested OS resource is denied, restricted or revoked.

Preconditions: Platform interaction must be present and relevant assets identified; no failure is assumed.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: Toggle only the test app permissions on the owned device and assess fallback, relaunch and recovery. Distinguish essential feature loss from an unintended app-wide failure.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://mas.owasp.org/MASVS/
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Handle denial/revocation and provide appropriate feature-specific fallback.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.

text.text:
P5 Android Keystore
Cryptographic key use

data.name:
P5 Android Keystore
Cryptographic key use
data.description: [PLATFORM FACT] OS service supports non-exportable keys and policy-controlled cryptographic operations. App use, authentication policy and hardware backing are unknown. Operations return results, not raw non-exportable key material. It is not a general token store. [CONDITIONAL] Flows apply only if observed or selected for investigation.

threats.title: ANDROID-PA-T26: A key operation succeeds outside its intended authorization state
threats.description:
Candidate scenario: If the app uses Keystore, a caller acting through the app may perform a protected cryptographic operation without the required user authority even though key material is non-exportable.

Preconditions: App Keystore use is established. Direct app compromise or privileged instrumentation is a distinct test variant, not the default attacker.

Tester-owned device evidence to seek: Establish app key use, then compare allowed operations across lock, authentication and account states. Confirm key policy/hardware backing only where evidence allows. A compromised-app variant requires separate stated access.

Knowledge: OS facility known; app use and configured policy unknown. No app-specific finding yet.
Reference: https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/keystore
threats.mitigation:
Proposed treatment: Bind sensitive key use to suitable authorization policy and validate operation purpose; non-exportability alone does not authorize an operation.

Closure: document actual environment, required privileges, observed behaviour and residual risk. Do not infer an internal cause from an external outcome alone.
